newsitem.title: UK: Base metals trading slow in LME evening.
newsitem.headline: Base metals trading slow in LME evening.

text.p: Base metal prices mostly showed little change during London Metal Exchange (LME) Friday evening inter-office trading.
Business was slow with only light book-squaring in copper prompting slight fluctuations in prices.
Traders said copper's performance over the past two days had broken an uptrend and from a technical point of view it would be no surprise if the market dipped further next week.

However, the unexpected fall in LME copper stocks on Friday may mean that a cautious attitude will be adopted as traders await next Tuesday's LME inventory data to see if the stocks downtrend continues, or whether it was just a one-off.
Other metals were likely to continue to be influenced by movements in the copper price
At 1800 GMT three months delivery copper was quoted at $1,930/1,933 a tonne compared with $1,932/1,933 at the 1600 GMT kerb close.
